about: When each campus shuttle line's buses are REALLY seen starting and ending service, bus by bus, compared with the timetable, and when a bus leaves one line to start another (a transition). Owner, 2026-11-11: "Refresh the end of service data in another file where each line is shown their daily seeming end and start time for each bus and transition (explain the reasoning in the same file)." Built by tools/build_service_seen.py from what Passio's public feed showed and what the collector logged; learned, unofficial, not a timetable: it says what usually happened, never what will happen. web/data/idle.json is a separate, older file (E28 linger spots).

fields.from, to, days_used: the service days used (a service day runs 04:00 to 04:00 Chicago time)
fields.days_left_out: days in the range not used, with why (holidays and breaks from data/calendar.json, missing data)
fields.collector_gaps: stretches with no poll at all (the collector was down); stints are not split across them, but a start or end inside one is read late or early
fields.valid_until: newest day + 45 days; after it, treat the file as stale (refresh it)
fields.lines.<route_id>.name: the line (GTFS route_id = the live feed's route_id)
fields.lines.<route_id>.days[]: one entry per day type: `type` (weekday, sat, sun, or a split such as mon-thu + fri), `dows` (the days of the week it covers: pick the entry whose dows include today), `days_total` (service days of that type in the range), `days_seen` (days a bus served the line), `split` (why the type was split, if it was)
fields.listed: the timetable's listed spans on those days ('HH:MM' service-day clock; 24:25 = 00:25 the next morning), from each day's own timetable; `days` = days with that listing (the most common one)
fields.seen: line level, per day then summarized: first_report (first fresh report under the line's label within an hour before a bus's first stop), first_stop (first logged arrival of any bus), last_stop (last logged arrival of any bus), last_report (last fresh report under the label within an hour after a bus's last stop); buses = shifts per day (p50, max)
fields.stat {p10, p50, p90, n}: service-day clock times: median (p50) and the 10th to 90th percentile spread over n days (linear interpolation; with fewer than 5 days p10 / p90 are about the earliest / latest day)
fields.vs_listed: start_late_min = median first stop - listed start; end_early_min = listed end - median last stop (positive = the buses stop before the listed end); days_ending_15_min_early; days_ending_after_listed
fields.buses[]: Bus 1, Bus 2, ... = the line's shifts of the day in the order they first reported under the line's label (NOT the app's Bus N labels, which follow vehicle numbers: web/js/core/busnum.js). Per bus: days (days the line had a k-th bus), first_report, first_stop, last_stop, last_report (stats), starts_at / ends_at (the most common first / last stop), breaks_days (days that bus took a break of 30 min to 3 h inside its shift), vehicle / vehicle_days (the bus number seen most in that slot)
fields.breaks[]: a line's usual breaks inside a shift (same line again 30 min to 3 h later), per stop where they start, seen on 3 days or more: from / to (stats of the break's start = the last stop before it, and end = the first stop after it), days, times, at / back_at (stops), vehicles (top 3, 'bus xdays')
fields.spans_seen: for a line listed twice a day (Midway Metra): per listed span, the seen first / last stop of the shifts that overlap it most and end_early_min (listed span end - median last stop)
fields.outside_listed: shifts seen under the line's label with under half their time inside the listed hours widened by 60 min (usually a bus that kept last night's label): counted here, never as a Bus k
fields.friday_vs_mon_thu: per line, Friday's median [first stop, last stop] minus Monday to Thursday's, in minutes (positive = later): the check for Friday nights
fields.transitions[]: a bus leaving one line and starting another within 3 h: from / to (route ids + names), day_type (of the from line), days (days seen) of of_days, times, kind (direct = median gap up to 30 min, after_break = longer), leave (its last stop on the from line), join (its first stop on the to line), gap_min (median), left_at / joined_at (stops) and left_at_ll / joined_at_ll ([lat, lon] of those stops), from_bus / to_bus (its order on each line that day), label_on_the_way (the label most of its reports between leave and join carried: from, to, other, or none = out of the feed), label_share, to_label_after_min (median minutes after leaving until it first reported under the new line's label), off_line_share (share of its reports on the way farther than 250 m from the drawn line of the label they carried: what the app's off-route rule measures; learned corridors not applied), unseen_on_the_way (times with no report at all on the way), vehicles (top 3)

method: Data: every archived service day from `from` to `to` (raw position polls = what the app's feed showed; each day's own timetable; the collector's logged arrivals, data branch data/ground_truth/arrivals.csv, every source). A report counts when it is at most 300 s older than its poll (web/js/core/operating.js).

A STINT = a bus's consecutive logged arrivals on one line with gaps of at most 30 min (or a collector gap); stints with fewer than 3 arrivals are dropped as noise (a pass under a wrong label) and the stints around them re-joined. Arrivals inside E30's wrong_line_label episodes (data/labeled/transitions/odd_episodes.csv: the bus drove another line under this label) are left out.

A SHIFT = one bus's stints on one line within 3 h of each other; the gaps of 30 min to 3 h inside it are its breaks; a return after more than 3 h is a new shift (a new Bus k). seen start = its first stop, seen end = its last stop; first / last report = its earliest / latest fresh report under the line's label up to an hour before / after (a bus deadheading from the garage, or lingering after its last trip, under the label).
Bus order: per line and day, the shifts sorted by first report (Bus 1 reported first). Each Bus k is then summarized over the days of the day type that had a k-th bus.

A TRANSITION = a bus's stint on line A followed by a stint on line B (B not A) within 3 h; leave = its last stop on A, join = its first stop on B. Grouped per (A, B, A's day type) and split where the leave clock times of consecutive cases are more than 60 min apart; kept when seen on 2 days or more.

Day types: weekday (Mon to Fri), Saturday, Sunday; split where the timetable lists different hours inside a type, and a single weekday is split off when its median first or last stop differs from the rest by 30 min or more (3 days or more on each side).
Holidays and breaks (data/calendar.json regimes holiday / break) are left out: the shuttles run a different service then. Reading period and finals are kept (same timetable).
why_seen_differs_from_listed: Listed ends outlast the service on every weekday (RouteKnower E30, service_end_early): the Downtown Campus Connector is listed to 00:25 but its last bus ends about 22:04 to 23:09; Apostolic/Drexel to 00:55 vs about 00:00 (the NightRide notice's end); 53rd Street Express to 19:25 vs about 18:10; Midway Metra's morning span to 11:55 vs about 10:00 on 20 of 22 weekdays.
Some listed buses never come: North's second bus from 21:00 was missing on 26 of 32 days (E30 timetable_add_missed); Friend Center/Metra's 05:00 weekend listing never runs (known since Oct 25).
NightRide (North, South, East) is listed to about 04:29 but Passio lists no bus after about midnight (the app says "No shuttles are reporting live locations" then; project notes 2026-10-10).
Some lines run past the listed end: Central (listed to 23:14) reports until about 23:30 to 00:00 on most nights (E30 after_hours).

The timetable is the operator's plan; Passio's feed shows the buses that actually report. A bus can also serve unseen (its tablet off): `days_seen` and the collector gaps say how much to trust a line's numbers.
layovers_vs_lasting: Between trips Passio leaves a bus out of the feed for 10 to 27 min (a layover), so a short silence is not the end of service. The same 30-min rule as the collector's bus count changes (tools/bus_changes.py LASTING_S, data/ground_truth/bus_changes.csv `lasting`: a dropped bus back on its line within 30 min is a layover, lasting = 0) joins a bus's arrivals into one stint; a longer gap on the same line (up to 3 h) is a break inside the shift (listed under breaks), and a move to another line is a transition. A bus's seen end is therefore its last stop before at least 3 h without serving the line, never a layover.
how_the_app_uses_it: Planned (display-rules work, 2026-11-11): (1) end of service for the idle rule: past a line's usual last stop (the last bus's last_stop p90, today's listed hours equal to `listed`), a still bus of the line is very likely done for the day; (2) transition windows: a bus off its new line's route between a transition's leave and join (from the from line's end spot, under the label shown in label_on_the_way) is on its way to start service, not lost. The app must check `valid_until` and that today's listed hours equal `listed.spans`, and never show these learned times as a schedule. Whoever wires it documents the use in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
refresh: Monthly, after a timetable change, or when valid_until passes (and after a holiday or a break, which are left out). Commands: python experiments/routeknower/E28-scripts/fetch.py --out <dl> --from 2026-10-10 --to <newest complete day>; python tools/build_service_seen.py --dl <dl> --odd data/labeled/transitions/odd_episodes.csv; python tools/test_service_seen.py. About 15 s for 32 days plus the downloads. The data repo's weekly findings run (github.com/blobberus/straight-bussing-data, findings/service_seen/service_seen.json) rebuilds a candidate copy every Monday: adopt it here after a look. docs/DATA.md "Seen service windows".
